thread:
jamie_support: URGENT — customer reports a large unexpected credit use overnight. Ticket #23456. Org 0xACME dropped from ~10,000 credits to ~200 after their nightly backfill (embeddings + rerank). Suspect duplicate calls from scheduler retries.

jamie_support: Paste of redacted logs: 
```
2026-03-16T00:01:02Z job=backfill id=job-789 worker=host-a request_id=req-111 POST /v1/embeddings 200 tokens=150
2026-03-16T00:01:03Z job=backfill id=job-789 worker=host-a callback=webhook POST /internal/callback 504
2026-03-16T00:01:05Z job=backfill id=job-789 worker=host-b reenqueue reason=callback_timeout
2026-03-16T00:01:06Z job=backfill id=job-789 worker=host-b request_id=req-112 POST /v1/embeddings 200 tokens=150
```

sam_ops: Can you confirm the job id and scheduler version that ran at midnight? Any other evidence of double-enqueue beyond this sample?

jamie_support: job-789, scheduler v1.12. Customer attached call counts showing ~2x embeddings calls per row. They also said their promo/trial didn’t apply for those runs.

bri_engineering: That trace looks like the scheduler re-enqueued after a callback 504. Are we forwarding idempotency tokens? Old workers set `Idempotency-Key`, new infra expects `x-idempotency-key`.

bri_engineering: Quick check: backfill client sets `Idempotency-Key: <job-789>` but the HTTP proxy normalizes headers and drops mixed-case ones in vproxy v0.9.0. If the proxy rewrites/drops the header, the second worker won't dedupe.

eng_oncall: Confirmed two separate hosts processed the same job id within ~4s. Matches a leader-election window where an ack path timed out. Looks like scheduler v1.12 + vproxy 0.9.0 combination.

elena_billing: If both requests used the org’s prod API key instead of the promo key, both were billed. Jamie 94 can you confirm which API key was sent and collect token counts for the hour so we can compute refund delta?

jamie_support: From logs (redacted): `X-API-Key: sk-live-0xACME` 94 so prod key. Customer thought promo was active but we don’t see promo flag on those calls. Org: 0xACME, window: 2026-03-16 00:00-01:00 UTC. Audit in progress.

deploybot: deploy vproxy@0.9.0 -> 0.9.1 rollback scheduled 2026-03-16T02:30Z for header-normalization bug. :rotating_light:

bri_engineering: Local repro steps I used:
1) start scheduler v1.12
2) run backfill client with `Idempotency-Key` header set to job id
3) simulate callback service returning 504 on first worker
Expected: second attempt dedupes if idempotency header preserved. Observed: header is lost -> duplicate embeddings calls.

bri_engineering: Patch plan: - normalize idempotency header in the client to `X-Idempotency-Key` and add server-side fallback to read both `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Idempotency-Key`. - add short-lived (30s) job-id dedupe at embeddings ingress as a safety net. Opening PR this morning.

sam_ops: Immediate mitigation options: pause nightly backfills for affected orgs via ops console toggle, or add a rate-limiter that rejects duplicate embeddings calls for same job id within 10m. I'll pause runs for org 0xACME now.

elena_billing: Once token counts are posted I'll compute the charge delta. Approving a one-off credit equal to excess tokens * token_price. Also will temporarily reapply the 30-day promo retroactively for the affected window to avoid surprise billing.

jamie_support: Audit sample: 1,200 rows processed -> expected ~180k tokens, observed billed ~360k tokens. ~180k tokens extra. Customer notified; refund plan + ops throttle in place. Ticket updated.

eng_oncall: Root cause: vproxy header normalization bug combined with a leader-election race that allowed duplicate worker execution. Mitigations: rollback vproxy, client header change, server-side dedupe; postmortem to follow.

jamie_support: Customer satisfied with refund + throttle. Keeping ticket open until client patch lands. :thumbsup:
